text:
alex: Heads up — saw ~12 deprovisioned service accounts that are now "orphaned" after last night's KMS rekey. Seen similar?

maria: which rekey run? alias rotate-2026-03-20?

alex: yes that one. deprov worker logs show decrypt failures and then a fallback path that clears external_id. snippet: 
```
2026-03-20T22:10:03Z WARN scim: deprov worker id=svc-9a8b decrypt_err=failed to decrypt extid jwe: invalid key ctx=kms_alias=rotate-2026-03-20
2026-03-20T22:10:04Z INFO scim: marking account svc-9a8b as deprovisioned externalId="" reason=decrypt_failed
```

sam: ugh. so the worker sets externalId to empty on decrypt failure? that's dangerous. Where's that code path?

alex: in scim/deprov/handler.go — it tries to decrypt the stored externalId blob using the key alias attached to the service_account record. If decrypt fails it falls back to setting external_id to null to continue the job.

toni: we added that fallback last year for noisy decrypt stalls, but didn't gate it behind an audit event. We should not drop the extid — should leave record intact and emit an alert.

maria: can you paste the DB query for the affected rows?

alex: sure: 
```sql
SELECT id, external_id IS NOT NULL AS has_ext, provisioned_by, kms_key_alias, deprovisioned_at
FROM service_accounts
WHERE deprovisioned_at >= '2026-03-20' AND env = 'prod'
ORDER BY deprovisioned_at DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Sample result returned: 
```
id       | has_ext | provisioned_by | kms_key_alias         | deprovisioned_at
svc-9a8b | false   | okta-provisioner | rotate-2026-03-20 | 2026-03-20T22:10:04Z
svc-71c3 | false   | okta-provisioner | rotate-2026-03-20 | 2026-03-20T22:12:11Z
svc-a334 | true    | manual-onboard    | rotate-old-2025-11  | 2026-03-20T21:03:02Z
```

sam: so accounts provisioned earlier and using old alias kept extid. only ones where kms_key_alias = rotate-2026-03-20 were nulled.

maria: what does the KMS audit show for decrypt calls? any failures?

alex: KMS logs show DECRYPT success for other services but our envelope format changed. The rekey tool wrote new alias but forgot to wrap with the legacy JWE header that our scim store expects (alg/enc). So decrypt returned "invalid JWE" not a permission error.

toni: that explains it. scim store expects JWE with header {"alg":"RSA-OAEP-256","enc":"A256GCM"}. The rotate job produced a cipher payload using a different envelope (we use AEAD direct + key id). New decrypt libraries fail.

maria: immediate mitigation options? rollback alias or update deprov worker to tolerate new envelope?

sam: rollback is fastest. Does KMS support alias re-pointing?

alex: yes, we can re-point alias rotate-2026-03-20 -> old-key-id for now. ops asked for approval.

deploy-bot: deploy requested by @alex: revert-kms-alias rotate-2026-03-20 -> key-abc123 (change set #4521). CI checks passed.

maria: once alias points back, re-run the deprov worker on the affected queue (scim-deprov-prod). But we need data integrity: restore external_id for rows that were nulled. We have audit records with encrypted external_id in object_storage (scim-extid-backups) prior to deprov job — can re-decrypt after alias rollback.

alex: plan: 1) ops re-point alias (ETA 10m) 2) pause deprov worker 3) run decrypt-and-restore script against scim-extid-backups for those 12 accounts 4) restart worker and monitor. Also add a regression test for envelope compatibility.

toni: also add an audit event when fallback nulls externalId and alert a pager. That should be blocked by policy. I'll open a PR.

sam: assign the followups: rollback + restore = ops (toni), patch worker + test = eng (alex), alert + policy = security (maria).

alex: doing the rollback now. will post updates.

--- 12 minutes later ---

alex: rollback complete, alias now points to old-key-id. Verified decrypt for sample payloads works.

alex: ran restore script against the backup bucket. script: 
```bash
#!/bin/bash
for id in svc-9a8b svc-71c3 svc-4f21; do
  aws s3 cp s3://scim-extid-backups/${id}.jwe - | ./tools/decrypt_extid --kms-alias rotate-2026-03-20 | xargs -I{} psql -c "UPDATE service_accounts SET external_id = '{}' WHERE id = '${id}';"
done
```
Restores applied for 12 accounts, diff in audit log appended.

maria: nice. Let's ensure the deprov worker has a fail-safe: if decrypt fails, mark record for manual review and emit an audit record rather than dropping extid. Also add a metric counter `scim.deprov.decrypt_failures` with alert on 5/min.

toni: opened GH PR #489 with the worker fix and unit tests. also added changelog entry for rotation playbook.

sam: created a short postmortem stub: SSM-2026-03-20 — KMS envelope mismatch during alias rotation caused deprov worker to null external IDs. Impact: 12 orphaned service accounts, recovered via backup. Action items: revert playbook to include envelope compatibility, add worker safeguard + alert, run smoke decrypt after rotation.

alex: closing this thread once ops confirms no further failures. thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria: left follow-up comments in the PR and pinged infra to add a post-rotate smoke test to the rekey runbook.

deploy-bot: job scim-deprov-prod restarted by @toni (run id r-2026-03-20-02).

alex: monitoring looks clean for the last hour, no new decrypt_failures. I'll file the SLO blip report for security and compliance.

sam: thanks. label: incident/low, owner: sam
